data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference is defensible only if we accept a 'decisionist' cost: rationality is not about tracking truth or probability, but about committing to a set of rules that define the scientific game, even if those rules have no external guarantee.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If scientists demand external validation (truth/probability) for their actions.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 'game' of science cannot sustain itself without inductive success.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the decision to play the game itself requires an inductive justification.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Popper's system ultimately rests on a foundational decision to value falsifiability and critical discussion.
